title: List connected GitHub sources
description: The team's selectable GitHub repositories, oldest source first: one entry per repository a source syncs, each with its source id, repo (owner/name), table prefix, and a synced flag. A source can sync several repositories, so entries can share an id and differ only by repo. Call this first when a team may have more than one source or repo, then pass a chosen entry's id as source_id AND its repo as repo to the pull-requests, workflow-health, ci-cards, or pr-lifecycle tools to read that specific repo: omitting repo on a multi-repo source reads the source's default repo, not the one you picked. With a single source/repo you can skip it: the other tools default to the oldest connected source. The prefix also names the underlying warehouse tables, which you can query directly with SQL or save as SQL insights and subscriptions when the named tools don't fit. The source's original repo uses bare names (prefix + github_pull_requests / github_workflow_runs / github_workflow_jobs); every other repo of a multi-repo source is repo-qualified: the name `owner/repo.endpoint` is flattened for the table (each '/' becomes '_' and each '.' becomes '__', lower-cased), e.g. posthog/posthog.com's pull_requests is prefix + github_posthog_posthog__com__pull_requests: so pick the table for the repo you mean (timestamps land as strings; parse with parseDateTimeBestEffort).

methodDocumentation.text: The team's selectable GitHub repositories, oldest source first: one entry per repository a source is configured to sync, so a source syncing several repositories appears once per repo. Populate a repo picker from this and pass a chosen entry's `id` back as `source_id` and its `repo` back as `repo` to the other endpoints. Includes repositories whose tables aren't fully synced yet.
